opportunities.title: [Bounty $3,000] Fix ttnn.sampling distribution bias from low-precision random threshold
opportunities.description:
# 📝 Background

This is a community-suggested bounty that we have reviewed and assigned to [@samiyadev786](https://github.com/samiyadev786).

`ttnn.sampling` is used for on-device non-greedy token sampling in the shared sampling path used by `tt-transformers` and other model integrations. The operation currently compares an FP32 cumulative probability against a random threshold that is packed to bfloat16. Because the threshold has only bfloat16 resolution, the sampler does not draw from the requested distribution accurately.

The issue has been reproduced on both Wormhole N150 and Blackhole P150. In the reported measurements, candidate tokens with small probabilities were never emitted or were emitted at materially incorrect frequencies. The existing tests primarily check candidate membership, determinism, and valid indices; they do not provide a sufficiently sensitive frequency-based regression test.

# 💡 Problem to Solve

Fix the random-threshold path in `ttnn.sampling` so that the threshold used by the comparison has sufficient FP32-level resolution across the supported Wormhole and Blackhole implementations.

The fix must preserve the existing public API and sampling controls,

## Problem

Public usage figures (`/api/metrics`, `/api/runs`, `/proof`) count every caller origin together. A reader cannot tell outside users from team activity or scripted acceptance runs, and scripted persona batches appear in the public run history next to real questions. A reviewer who opens the run history sees bursts of templated questions and discounts all of it, including the genuine use.

## Proposal

One public page and one JSON endpoint that answer "who uses Keryx" from the production database on every load.

- Three columns for every figure: **outside users**, **team**, **scripted tests**. Never summed silently.
- One network at a time: Arc mainnet and Arc testnet reported separately.
- Period switch: all time, last 7 days, last 30 days, and `?since=YYYY-MM-DD`.
- Rows: people, research runs, paying runs, settled payments, USDC paid, creators paid, deliverables accepted, median time to first answer.
- Classify at write time, not after the fact: a run created by an evaluation harness or a team wallet carries an origin tag when it is stored.

opportunities.title: Agent CLI node-status exits success for an invalid blockchain-list response
opportunities.description:
`node-status` reports success when the HTTP-200 blockchain list cannot be decoded or does not have the expected shape. The Python parser failure is swallowed by `|| true`, after which an empty `chains` value is treated as a legitimate empty configuration.

Affected: [`cmd_node_status`, lines 990–999 at current main `8b3b564`](https://github.com/PayRam/payram-scripts/blob/8b3b56487ff2a9f34822ba77bd4d3f78e1db7bf6/setup_payram_agents.sh#L990-L999).

Expected: an invalid list produces a nonzero exit and an explicit inability to determine node health. A valid empty list or genuinely inactive configuration can retain the current success result.

Observed: all four invalid fixtures below exit **0** and print `No active chains configured.`. A script using `node-status` as a health gate therefore receives the same success status as a valid empty configuration, even though no chain health was established.

| Local HTTP-200 fixture | Original exit | Patched exit |
|---|---:|---:|
| Valid active BASE chain, running listener and fresh connected node | 0 | 0 |
| Valid empty list `[]` | 0 | 0 |
| Valid inactive BASE chain | 0 | 0 |
| HTML instead of JSON | 0 | 1 |
| Truncated JSON list | 0 | 1 |

opportunities.title: Reliability: specify and test crash recovery across replay consumption and chain append
opportunities.description:
[The hardening report](https://github.com/rickyjreyes/Wavelock/blob/master/audit/BOUNTY_HARDENING_REPORT.md) records separate durable replay consumption and block append. A crash can burn a key without storing its block; interrupted JSONL writes can prevent loading. Rebuilding accepted identities from the chain does not recover every burned identity.

- [ ] Specify crash states and safe operator recovery for signer, replay, and chain files.
- [ ] Provide a recovery procedure or tool that preserves consumed identities and does not silently truncate authenticated history or authorize reuse.
- [ ] Add fault-injection coverage at each relevant write boundary, including partial tails and restart.
- [ ] Demonstrate normal continuation after recovery or a clear fail-closed diagnostic when recovery cannot be established.

This is availability/recovery work. Key burning without invalid acceptance is not a Public Bounty v1 exploit.

This ticket tracks outstanding work; it does not report a newly reproduced vulnerability. Preserve existing protocol versions, reference vectors, and the `v0.2.0` tag. Any new protocol behavior requires explicit versioning and review.

opportunities.title: Roadmap: define and implement cross-node agreement for consumed OTS identities
opportunities.description:
[The Merkle roadmap](https://github.com/rickyjreyes/Wavelock/blob/master/docs/WAVELOCK_MERKLE_ROADMAP.md) explicitly leaves cross-node replay-ledger replication open. Current locks and reconstruction enforce consistency on a shared host/filesystem; independently operated nodes do not obtain global agreement from those locks.

- [ ] Specify the public network threat model, authoritative chain/finality rules, and replay-state derivation.
- [ ] Define behavior for competing blocks, partitions, reconnects, restart, and reorganization.
- [ ] Implement the approved agreement mechanism without treating ledger copying alone as consensus.
- [ ] Add multi-node tests showing the same identity cannot be finalized twice under the declared assumptions, with partition and restart scenarios.
- [ ] Document compatibility and deployment requirements.

This is future scope and is not a failure of Public Bounty v1's same-host AR-6 promise.

This ticket tracks outstanding work; it does not report a newly reproduced vulnerability. Preserve existing protocol versions, reference vectors, and the `v0.2.0` tag. Any new protocol behavior requires explicit versioning and review.

opportunities.title: Research: establish explicit hardness and binding claims beyond regression evidence
opportunities.description:
[Candidate B restricted binding](https://github.com/rickyjreyes/Wavelock/blob/master/docs/CC_CORE_V1_RESTRICTED_BINDING.md) leaves general trajectory uniqueness and inversion hardness unresolved. [PDE results](https://github.com/rickyjreyes/Wavelock/blob/master/docs/PDE_HASH_RESULTS.md) contain no lower bound on attack cost. Public Bounty v1 C1/C2 likewise have `security_proof: NONE`; these are distinct constructions and must not share claims by implication.

- [ ] State separate security games, input distributions, attacker access, and work/memory accounting for each construction under study.
- [ ] Identify what existing theorems establish and the exact missing lemmas for any proposed reduction or lower bound.
- [ ] Adversarially review proposed arguments, including digest-level re-merging and computation shortcuts.
- [ ] Publish a reproducible research checkpoint: proved conditional result, counterexample, or explicit unresolved obligations with bounded evidence.

Completion of a research checkpoint must not be relabeled a full security proof. Absence of a proof alone is not a qualifying bounty exploit.
